title: Verify host cache, runtime and system package files through the file that is read
summary: The host cache launcher (`scripts/ia.mjs`, which verifies the cache before every mode), `installedDistributionDigest` and `verifySystemPackage` now open each file before judging it, read it through that descriptor, and check afterwards that its name still holds the same file. A file replaced while they verify by a link, FIFO, socket or other special file is refused: where the platform has `O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_NONBLOCK`, at the open, before anything is read, so the launcher no longer waits forever on a FIFO swapped into the cache; on Windows, which has neither, a link swapped in is opened and read, then refused by the check of its name. The launcher reports such a change with its own message rather than a system error such as `Unknown system error -102`; of the failures that keep a file from opening, it prints the system error only for a pinned file it may not read. A pinned cache file removed during verification reports `Plugin cache payload is missing`, and any other entry whose listed name no longer reaches it, such as a file Linux lists under a name that is not UTF-8, refuses as `Plugin cache payload differs: <path>`, where it failed with a system error before. Outside such races, which files are admitted is unchanged. Some refusals are new: `installedDistributionDigest` refuses a runtime file it cannot open, an unreadable one included, and an entry its listed name no longer reaches with `Installed distribution runtime is missing, mixed or aliased` instead of a system error; the launcher refuses a pinned file that fails to open for a reason other than permissions, such as too many open files or a lock another Windows process holds, as `Plugin cache payload differs: <path>`; `verifySystemPackage` refuses an input replaced or changed while it is read with `System package input changed while it was read: <path>`; and both refuse a file of more than 2147483647 bytes before reading it, `installedDistributionDigest` with its usual message and `verifySystemPackage` as `System package input exceeds 2147483647 bytes: <path>`, where Node's own error for a file that large was thrown.
